extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy/history of science (readers of Bacon's Novum Organum)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Francis Bacon's criteria for good scientific method and for judging philosophies/experiments (as presented in Novum Organum and Spedding's notes). Focuses on faults to avoid, positive methodological prescriptions, and signs of weak vs. strong philosophical systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senses frequently fail or deceive
rubrics_metrics.description: The senses frequently fail or deceive us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize sensory deficiencies as a primary defect of current demonstration; provide substitutions (instruments) and rectifications (methods) to correct sense errors rather than discarding sensory data wholesale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notions are confused and ill-defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Our notions are confused and ill-defined (notiones ... interminatae et confusae).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to abstract clear, well‑bounded concepts from impressions; ensure notions are 'terminatas et bene finitas' before using them in inference or theory-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Inductio per Enumerationem Simplicem
rubrics_metrics.description: We employ the vicious method of Inductio per Enumerationem Simplicem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simple enumeration yields merely empirical laws unfit beyond specific circumstances; instead use eliminative/structured inductive procedures (see tables of presence/absence, praerogativae instantiarum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid leaping at once to the most general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: We fly off at once to the principia maxime generalia, instead of ascending gradually through axiomata intima and media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ascend stepwise from particular observations to intermediate axioms and only then to broad principles to avoid error from premature abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undue extension of inferences to apparently similar instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Undue extension of inferences based on experience to other instances apparently similar, without sufficient caution in allowing for possible differences of circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overgeneralizing from limited cases; require careful matching of material circumstances before inferring recurrence of results (e.g., medicinal effects vary by climate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hap‑hazard (orderless) experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hap‑hazard experiment, without pursuing any definite order or making any selection of instances (mera palpatio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt Experientia Literata (directed, orderly experimentation) rather than undirected trial; design experiments with selection and systematic sequence so they build cumulative knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient variation of experiments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adequate variation across conditions to test hypotheses broadly rather than repeating near‑identical cases; prevents artefactual conclusions from narrow sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overfixation on a single experiment or subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuit of one experiment, or subject, to the neglect of all others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid concentrating all effort on a single line of inquiry at the expense of wider investigation (examples: Gilbert on magnet, Chymici on gold). Distribute inquiry to apprehend general patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive eagerness for premature practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive eagerness to arrive at the practical application (praxin) leading to premature deflection from pure inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist the temptation to prioritize immediate utility over careful verification; practical aims should follow, not precede, robust causal discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer method of elimination / tables of instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of elimination: draw up tables of presence, absence, etc., and reject out of all possible explanations until a residuum (true cause/form) remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct presence/absence tables and use eliminative reasoning; if more than one candidate remains, refine via praerogativae instantiarum and other 'aids of the understanding' until the form is isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bind demonstration to the experiment itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration is best when it adheres to the experiment itself; translation to other cases is fallacious unless done rightly and in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep demonstrative claims anchored in the experimental context; when generalizing, perform ordered and justified transfer to similar cases to avoid 'fallax' inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek 'lucifera' (light‑bearing) experiments over merely 'fructifera'
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek lucifera experimenta (light‑bearing experiments) which elicit causes and axioms, not merely fructifera (fruitful) practical experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experiments that illuminate underlying causes and generate axioms (which later furnish many practical applications) rather than only those that produce immediate useful effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge philosophies by their fruits (practical results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter signa, nullum magis certum aut nobile est, quam quod ex fructibus. Fructus et opera inventa pro veritate philosophiarum velut sponsos et fidejussores sunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practical outcomes, inventions, and operable results as primary evidence for the truth or value of a philosophical system; sterile disputation without fruits indicates weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use increment/progress as a sign of sound doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Capienda etiam sunt signa ex incrementis et progressibus philosophiarum. Quae in natura fundata sunt, crescunt et augentur: quae autem in opinione, variantur, non augentur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a doctrine shows sustained growth and cumulative improvement (characteristic of nature‑based sciences) versus mere variation of opinion (which shows little or no real advancement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of origin/time/location as decisive signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs taken from origin, nation, time, or age (ex ortu et gente, natura temporis et aetatis) are poor indicators of truth — e.g., Greek origin alone should not determine acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely primarily on pedigree, nationality, or antiquity as proof of truth; such historical signs are weak compared to empirical fruits and progress (though Bacon himself criticizes Greek bias).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply substitutions and rectifications by instruments and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitutions are to be supplied mainly by instruments, the rectifications mainly by methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct sense‑defects via instrumental aids (magnifiers, accurate measures) and cognitive/methodological errors via improved procedures and protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify wide a priori hypotheses before accepting them
rubrics_metrics.description: Fault lies not so much in framing wide hypotheses, as in taking them for ascertained truths and not insisting on their due verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat grand or abstract hypotheses as provisional until they have been rigorously tested; avoid adopting a priori systems without empirical confirmation.
